title: A chapter named for despair
hook: Arjuna drops his bow and sits down, and the Gita calls it a yoga
carry: the teaching starts when despair asks for help
tomorrow: the Isha's first line: does God live in it all, or clothe it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, reading the Gita's first chapter: kuladharmah, dharma that lives in what a family keeps, and Arjuna afraid a war will end it. Now the chapter reaches its last verse.

Anyone who has ended up on a bedroom floor beside something unfinished, phone face down, already knows how chapter one of the Gita ends. No battle. A man sits down. Arjuna lowers himself onto the floor of his chariot and lets his bow go. That much is plain. The puzzle comes one line later, in the label the chapter wears at its end. It calls all of this a yoga. The yoga of Arjuna's despair. Why would anyone name a collapse that way?
screen: `THE BEDROOM FLOOR.` → `NO BATTLE. A MAN SITS DOWN.` → `WHY CALL DESPAIR A YOGA?`

segments.voice: First the verse: evam uktvarjunah sankhye rathopastha upavishat, visrijya sasharam chapam shokasamvignamanasah. Uktva: having spoken. Visrijya: having let go. Upavishat: he sat down. Having spoken, having let go of his bow and arrows, he sat down, shokasamvignamanasah, his mind shaken by grief. Then comes a closing line that isn't part of the dialogue, the chapter's colophon, its label. It ends: arjunavishadayogo nama prathamo 'dhyayah. The yoga of Arjuna's despair, the first chapter. Vishada is despair, and the chapter is named for it. Now the teaching. The Gita doesn't open with a calm saint. It opens with the greatest archer of his age, unable to go on. And at the start of chapter two, still shaken, Arjuna says to Krishna: I am your student; I've come to you; teach me. Everything Krishna says after that, all the chapters Hindus learn by heart, is the answer to that moment. Many teachers read the label's word yoga this way: the despair is where the path begins, because it's what turns Arjuna into a student. Others hear yoga simply as the heading each chapter wears. Either way, the Gita's teaching starts on the floor of a chariot, with a man who asked for help.
screen: `UKTVA, VISRIJYA, UPAVISHAT: SPOKE, LET GO, SAT DOWN.` · `VISHADA: THE CHAPTER'S NAME.` · `CHAPTER TWO: TEACH ME.` · `THE PATH STARTS ON THE FLOOR.`

segments.voice: Sit down fully, the way Arjuna does, and let your hands rest open on your knees, as if something heavy has just been set down. Let the shoulders drop on each out-breath. If you pray, ask for help in your own words, the way Arjuna turned to Krishna. If you don't, name one person you could ask.
Reading the Gita's first chapter, to its last line: upavishat, he sat down, and vishada, despair, the name the chapter carries.
